name: Wen Xiaoqiong
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Wen Xiaoqiong (温小琼) is one of the Wen family members named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Wens was founded by her father Wen Beiying (per press reports) in 1983. She was among the top pre-IPO individual shareholders and is a passive shareholder rather than a manager.
interesting_fact: Wens began in 1983 when Wen Beiying raised 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong to start a chicken farm; it became China's largest livestock company, listing in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private; no public profile. Listed among Wens actual controllers in the 2023 annual report. Only route is the Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn). Hurun listing was shared with Chen Jianxing (also a listed controller).

name: Sun Fen
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Sun Fen (孙芬) is listed in Wens Foodstuff Group's annual reports as one of the Wen family members who are joint actual controllers of the company, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Her wealth derives from that shareholding; she holds no disclosed management position.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 1983 chicken farm funded with 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong into China's largest livestock group, listed in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private, no public profile; exact family relationship not confirmed in sources checked. Hurun listing shared with Wen Zhifen (Wens chairman/legal representative). Route via Wens board office.

name: Sir Rocco Forte
current_role: Chairman, Rocco Forte Hotels (London-based luxury hotel group; 49% owned by Saudi PIF since 2024)
profile: Son of Lord (Charles) Forte, Rocco Forte became CEO of the Forte Group in 1992 but lost it to Granada's £3.87bn hostile bid in 1995. He started again in 1996 with Brown's (London) and The Balmoral (Edinburgh), building Rocco Forte Hotels with sister Olga Polizzi. In 2023-24 Saudi PIF bought 49% at a ~£1.4bn valuation to fund expansion.
interesting_fact: After losing his father's empire in one of Britain's most bitter takeovers, he rebuilt a luxury group from scratch; in 2001 the Forte trademark was returned to him, and he and Olga Polizzi won the Cateys 2026 International Outstanding Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: He read modern languages at Pembroke College, Oxford, where he won a blue for fencing, and qualified as a chartered accountant in 1969 before joining the family business; he is also UK patron of Les Clefs d'Or, the society of hotel concierges.
notes: Media-friendly and outspoken (Brexit, UK tax policy); gives interviews regularly. Company press page blocks automated access; use the press/media section of roccofortehotels.com for the current PR contact. Head office 70 Jermyn Street, London (company office).

name: Guo Miaobo
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party of the controlling group of Guangdong Chant Group (SZSE: 002616); holds no position at the company
profile: Guo Miaobo (郭妙波) is the spouse of Chant Group chairman He Qiqiang and one of the parties acting in concert with the company's actual controllers (He Qiqiang and Mai Zhenghui), per the 2025 annual report. Chant, based in Zhongshan, Guangdong, started in gas appliances and has expanded into biomass and waste-to-energy power generation and industrial-park heat supply.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from making gas stoves and water heaters into environmental energy, operating agricultural-biomass power plants and waste-to-energy and heat-supply projects in China, a possible angle for an energy podcast.
notes: Private, non-executive; the 2025 annual report states she holds no post at Chant. Better interview target would be chairman He Qiqiang; route via the board secretary office (dmof@chantgroup.cn).

name: Sun Feng
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and Board Secretary, Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic Co. (SSE: 603283)
profile: Sun Feng (孙丰, b. 1978) founded Secote in Suzhou in June 2007 and still runs it as chairman and GM. Secote makes automated assembly and inspection equipment for consumer electronics makers and has expanded into semiconductor wafer inspection equipment. He and co-controller Zeng Hui are the company's actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a listed-company chairman, Sun Feng also personally serves as Secote's board secretary, the officer responsible for investor relations and disclosure.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote he started out as a test engineer at Kunshan KONE Elevator (昆山通力电梯), then ran a small automation equipment factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong development zone.
notes: Since he is also board secretary, the securities office email (zqb@secote.com) reaches his own office. Low English-language profile.

name: Huang Bo
current_role: Sole shareholder of Hong Kong-registered Hanjia Development Ltd (漢加發展), which holds ~9.5% of Hangzhou Atexco (Honghua Digital, SSE STAR: 688789); no management role disclosed
profile: Huang Bo (黄波, female) is an investor whose wealth comes from her holding company Hanjia Development, the second-largest shareholder of Atexco, a Hangzhou maker of industrial digital inkjet textile printers and inks. Atexco is controlled by chairman Jin Xiaotuan; Huang Bo is a passive shareholder.
interesting_fact: Atexco makes digital inkjet printing systems that replace traditional screen-printing in textile dyeing, and in 2023 bought 67% of ink supplier Tianjin Jingli to integrate ink production.
notes: Atexco's 2025 annual report identifies 'Huang Bo (黄波) 女士' as sole shareholder of Hanjia Development (9.54%). Essentially no public profile; common name, so be careful not to confuse with others. Only route is via Atexco's securities office.

name: Wang Yanan
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Lu Yuanjian) of Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon Co. (SZSE: 300174); holds no current post at the company
profile: Wang Yan'an (王延安, b. 1949) co-built Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon in Nanping, Fujian, with her husband Lu Yuanjian; she was general manager of the predecessor company and later a director and deputy GM. Yuanli is one of China's largest wood-based activated carbon producers and has moved into silica and carbon materials for new energy uses. She has since stepped back from any role.
interesting_fact: Yuanli's activated carbon business has expanded beyond water and food purification into materials for the battery/new-energy supply chain, such as porous carbon used in silicon-carbon anodes.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into industry she was a schoolteacher, teaching in the Wangtai school district and at a vocational school in Nanping, Fujian, before becoming GM of Nanping Yuanli Active Carbon, the company's predecessor.
notes: Name in Chinese is 王延安 (Wang Yan'an). Retired from company roles per the 2025 annual report; very low profile. The energy-materials angle may suit the podcast; route via board office dm@yuanlicarbon.com.

name: Zhang Guoxing
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2010-2013 with Zhang Guoping for 'Shenda' (soft plastics). This most likely refers to Jiangsu Shenda Group, a privately held BOPP/plastic film maker whose president is Zhang Guoping, but no source checked confirms Zhang Guoxing's role there.
interesting_fact: Jiangsu Shenda Group, a leading Chinese biaxially-oriented film producer, set up Yangzhou Boheng New Energy Materials to mass-produce current-collector base film for lithium batteries (per its machinery supplier Brückner).
notes: Identity unconfirmed; dropped off Hurun after 2013. Not related to Shanghai Shenda (600626, state-linked). If pursuing, the company's battery-film business (Zhang Guoping) is the more visible route.

name: Alan A. Ades (via Alan Ades 2014 GRAT)
current_role: Principal, Rugby Realty Co. (NJ); co-founder and principal owner, A & E Stores, Inc.; former Organogenesis director (2003-June 2025)
profile: The record 'Ades 2014 Grat Alan' is the Alan Ades 2014 GRAT, a trust of which Alan A. Ades (b. ~1939) is trustee; it is part of the Ades/Erani/Nussdorf group that controls Organogenesis (NASDAQ: ORGO), a regenerative-medicine/wound-care company. Ades co-founded retailer A & E Stores in 1966, ran it as CEO until 2020, and founded Rugby Realty in 1980.
interesting_fact: Ades was Organogenesis' chair and a director from 2003, when his family group backed the pioneer of FDA-approved living-cell skin substitutes (Apligraf) after its bankruptcy; he left the board in June 2025, and his son Robert remains a director.
deep_cut_fact: Before a five-decade retail career he earned a law degree (LL.B.) from NYU School of Law, after a B.A. in business administration from the University of Michigan; he then led A & E Stores as CEO for 54 years (1966-2020).
notes: Name in source data is a trust entity, not a person. Ades is ~87 and private; did not stand for re-election in 2025. Organogenesis contacts are company channels, not his own; Rugby Realty has no published press contact found. The 2003 Apligraf rescue detail is from general knowledge of company history; the board dates are from SEC filings.

name: George Mohan Zhang
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Crastal Technology Co. (Buydeem, 北鼎股份, SZSE: 300824)
profile: George Mohan Zhang (张默涵, b. 1982, Canadian national) has run Shenzhen Crastal Technology as chairman and GM since 2003. The company began as an OEM/ODM maker of small kitchen appliances and built its own premium brand, BUYDEEM, selling health kettles, steam ovens, water dispensers and toasters. He and Zhang Bei are the actual controllers; it listed in Shenzhen in 2020.
interesting_fact: He took the helm of the company in 2003 at about 21, and turned a contract manufacturer into a design-led consumer brand (BUYDEEM) sold in China and overseas.
deep_cut_fact: He studied mathematics and computing science (BSc) at Simon Fraser University in Vancouver and earned a master's in industrial engineering at UC Berkeley, as did his deputy GM Fang Zhen.
notes: English-speaking, North America-educated founder of a consumer brand, so a possible fit for an entrepreneurship episode. Route via the company's board office (buydeem@crastal.com).

name: Feng Yuexiu
current_role: No current role found; formerly director, legal representative and co-actual controller of Jiangsu Huasheng Tianlong Photoelectric (ChiNext: 300029, since delisted)
profile: Feng Yuexiu (冯月秀, b. 1948) was a co-founder-family controller and legal representative of Changzhou-based Tianlong Photoelectric, a maker of monocrystalline silicon growth furnaces, ingot furnaces and wafer-cutting equipment for the solar industry, which listed on ChiNext in 2009. Her Hurun ranking (2010-11) came from that stake. The company's stock has since been delisted (now '天龙退').
interesting_fact: Tianlong Photoelectric was an early Chinese maker of crystal-growth furnaces for solar silicon, and in 2011 formed a JV with a Hong Kong firm to develop MOCVD equipment for LEDs.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a solar-equipment entrepreneur she worked at the Exi (western Hubei) Chemical Plant from 1969 to 1974 and then spent 23 years (1975-1998) at the Changzhou No. 4 Radio Factory.
notes: Off the rich lists since 2011; low profile and no current public role. The listed company is delisted, so there's no reliable IR channel for her. Solar-equipment history fits the energy theme, but she is likely hard to reach.

name: Ségolène Moyrand-Gros
current_role: President (and CEO), Gattefossé Group, Saint-Priest/Lyon, France
profile: Ségolène Moyrand-Gros (b. 1981) is the fifth generation to lead Gattefossé, a family-owned Lyon company founded in 1880 that makes lipid-based pharmaceutical excipients and cosmetic active ingredients. She joined in 2006, sat on the board from 2013 and succeeded her father Jacques Moyrand as president in May 2021. She is pushing international growth, including a production site in Texas.
interesting_fact: Gattefossé is the birthplace of 'aromatherapy': company chemist-owner René-Maurice Gattefossé coined the term in the 1930s, and the firm's 1930-1950 history centres on lipid chemistry, dermatology and aromatherapy.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming president she worked her way through international marketing and Group Communication Manager roles, and from 2019 headed CSR for the whole group on the executive committee. She studied at ESCE and IAE Lille (industrial marketing) and took an Executive MBA at EM Lyon.
notes: Media-accessible: has given interviews (Personal Care Magazine, Le Journal des Entreprises) and appeared on the French podcast 'L'entreprise familiale nouvelle génération' (podcast.ausha.co/l-entreprise-familiale-nouvelle-generation/gattefosse). Gattefossé's contact page routes to a press contact form. Net worth reflects the founding family's shared stake.

name: Ye Xiangwu
current_role: Former chairman/GM and controlling shareholder of Hunan Jingfeng Pharmaceutical (SZSE: 000908); no current post at the company
profile: Ye Xiangwu (叶湘武) built Shanghai Jingfeng Pharmaceutical (景峰; Hurun's 'Jingfeng' is a romanisation variant of 京丰) and took it public in 2014-15 via a reverse merger into Hunan Tianyi Technology, then served as chairman and GM. The group made injectables and specialty drugs. After a court-supervised restructuring completed in March 2026, CSPC Holdings became controlling shareholder (now 石药集团湖南景峰医药).
interesting_fact: He took Jingfeng public through a 2014 reverse merger with Hunan Tianyi Technology, turning a Shanghai drugmaker into a Shenzhen-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: Before Jingfeng he was chairman and general manager of Guizhou Yibai Pharmaceutical (贵州益佰制药), another listed drugmaker; he holds a master's degree.
notes: Sensitive: the company went through restructuring and control passed to CSPC in 2026, so avoid the topic in outreach. The 2025 report says he holds no post at the company (a relative, Ye Gaojing, is a director). Company IR is no longer his channel. Listed with no country; he is a PRC national.
